cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet in Judah, has just heard the LORD announce disaster coming on Jerusalem (Jeremiah 15:1-9). Now he cries out about his own life. "Woe to me, my mother, that you have borne me, a man of strife and conflict in all the land."

cards.question: Jeremiah says everyone curses him over money he lent or borrowed.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks. He says He will surely deliver Jeremiah for a good purpose.

cards.question: The LORD says that in the time of trouble and distress, He will intercede with the enemy.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks a question. Can anyone smash iron, iron from the north, or bronze?

cards.question: The LORD asks if anyone can smash iron from the north, or bronze. What answer is that question pointing to?

answers.text: Only a king can smash it
Anyone with fire can smash it

cards.text: Then the LORD's words turn. He says wealth and treasures will be given up as plunder, without charge.

cards.question: The LORD says the wealth and treasures will be given up as plunder for all your ___.
Next the LORD says His anger will kindle a fire, and "you" will be enslaved to the enemies. Where?

answers.text: In a land you do not know
In the courts of the temple

cards.text: Now Jeremiah turns back to God. "You understand, O LORD; remember me and attend to me."

cards.question: Jeremiah asks the LORD to do something about his persecutors. What is it?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah asks the LORD, in His patience, not to take him away.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD he endures reproach for his own honor.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah talks about the LORD's words. He says they were found.

cards.question: When the LORD's words were found, what does Jeremiah say he did with them?
Jeremiah says the LORD's words became a heavy burden he could hardly carry.

cards.text: The Millers used to steal cookie dough right off my counter, but I never once saw anybody EAT the RECIPE. Then Jeremiah tells the LORD, "For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts."
Jeremiah says he never sat with the band of revelers, and he never celebrated with them.

cards.question: Jeremiah tells the LORD that because the LORD's hand was on him, he sat ___.

cards.text: Then he adds, "for You have filled me with indignation."
Jeremiah asks why his pain is unending and his wound won't heal. Then he tells the LORD what He has become like to him.

cards.question: Jeremiah says the LORD has become like what to him?

cards.text: A mirage, water that isn't there. Friend, that's raw honesty, and he's saying it straight to God.
So the LORD answers him. And His answer starts with an if.

cards.question: The LORD says that if Jeremiah returns, He will restore him, and Jeremiah will stand in His presence.

cards.text: Then comes a second if. This one's about the words coming out of Jeremiah's mouth.

cards.question: What kind of words does the LORD say Jeremiah must speak to be His spokesman?
The LORD tells Jeremiah that the people must turn to him, but he must not turn to them.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Jeremiah what He will make him to this people. A wall.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make Jeremiah a fortified wall of ___ to this people.
The LORD says the people won't even try to fight against Jeremiah.
The people will fight against Jeremiah, but the LORD says they won't overcome him. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD is with him to save him
The people are too afraid of him
The king's guards will protect him

cards.text: And the LORD's not done promising. He has one more line for Jeremiah, about the wicked and the ruthless.

cards.question: In His last line, what does the LORD promise to do for Jeremiah against the wicked and the ruthless?

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is almost never funny. Across 34 cards there is one real joke (stop 1 card 17). The other story cards read as plain narration or as a mild reaction, such as stop 2 card 3's "that's raw honesty." The passage gives him clear chances for a laugh, like Jeremiah wishing he'd never been born, getting cursed when he never lent or borrowed, and sitting alone while everyone else parties.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Many story cards are stripped-down paraphrase with no voice and almost no content: card 3, card 5 ("Then the LORD asks a question..."), card 7, card 12, card 14 ("He says they were found."), card 18 and card 20. Several of them only restate what the choice card right after them asks.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 15:16 says the LORD's words "became my joy and my heart's delight." This is never actually told. Card 16 only has the baker mark "a heavy burden" as false, and card 17 moves straight to the joke and "I bear Your name." A baker can leave without knowing the words became his joy, which is a key turn in the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer "In a land you do not know" is a general, Bible-sounding phrase. The two wrong answers are specific named places. This makes the right answer stand out. Also, "the courts of the temple" is not a believable place to be enslaved to enemies.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to pick the exact adjective pair (noble instead of worthless) from other pairs that are just as reasonable (gentle instead of harsh, humble instead of proud). Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason toward "noble." This is guessing the wording of the line, not its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answer "Deliver and redeem him" uses the passage's own verbs, and the baker has just seen "save and deliver" in verse 20 and "to save him" in card 12's right answer. The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out as the Bible-sounding one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Card 3 names Jeremiah as the "you" of verse 11 ("deliver Jeremiah"). In verses 13 and 14, the "you" is given over to plunder "for all your sins" and enslaved in a strange land, but cards 7 to 9 leave that "you" open and never mark a shift. Coming right after card 3, the baker will likely think Jeremiah himself is being plundered and enslaved for his sins. The text does not mark who the "you" is in verses 13 and 14.
findings.question: When a speech changes who "you" is without saying so, and leaving it open will likely lead the baker to the wrong person, should Papa Dorin say plainly that the text doesn't say who "you" is here? Or should card 3 also leave the "you" of verse 11 open?
